newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Litvinov refinery closed down.
newsitem.headline: Czech Litvinov refinery closed down.

text.p: Crude oil processing at the Czech Litvinov oil refinery has been completely halted due to a blaze at the plant on Saturday, owner Ceska Rafinerska a.s. said.

"The processing refinery has been closed down," Ceska Rafinerska spokesman Ales Soukup told Reuters. "But there is no damage to the unit," he said, adding that production would stepped up at its other refinery at Kralupy, north of Prague, to compensate.
"Part of the production of motor fuel has been transferred to the Kralupy refinery," he said. However, he did not make clear if Kralupy had enough capacity to compensate fully for Litvinov's closure.
Three firemen were injured in the blaze, which broke out at a pumping station shortly after midnight (2300 GMT Friday).
"It has been possible to stop the main part of the leak of fuel on to the site of the fire," he said. "Until now, however, fuel is flowing from two storage tanks and the fuel is burning."

In a deal completed in February this year, a consortium of Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco of the United States, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip SpA, bought a 49 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska a.s., a company set up to operate the oil refineries at Litvinov and Kralupy.
